data.title: Cultural Attaché in the U.S.: 26 Projects by Saudi Scholarship Students, Including Four Inventions with Patent Applications Filed
data.content:
Washington, November 21, 2026, SPA -- Saudi Cultural Attaché in the United States Dr. Tahani Al-Baiz affirmed that the scientific, research, and innovative achievements presented by Saudi scholarship students at American universities reflect a shift in the scholarship program, moving beyond mere academic attainment toward knowledge production, technological development, and the creation of new opportunities.
    This statement was made on the occasion of Minister of Education Yousef Al-Benyan's visit to the Bright Minds Showcase 2026—an exhibition of innovations by scholarship students, organized by the Saudi Cultural Attaché’s Office in the U.S. The visit was also attended by Deputy Minister for International Cooperation Dr. Latifa Al-Faryan and the accompanying delegation.
    In a statement to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA), Dr. Al-Baiz noted that the exhibition featured 26 scientific and innovative entries. These included four inventions for which the creators have filed U.S. patent applications, 12 entrepreneurship projects and initiatives, and three diverse educational and community-focused initiatives. She highlighted that these achievements span fields such as artificial intelligence, medical and biotechnologies, advanced engineering, environmental sustainability, education, and entrepreneurship—underscoring the breadth of contributions made by Saudi scholarship students and the wide scope of their scientific and research excellence. Cultural Attaché explained that these achievements are the fruit of the wise leadership's investment in developing human capital. She emphasized that scholarship students are no longer merely recipients of knowledge; rather, they have become partners in its production and the development of its applications—capable of transforming scientific research outcomes into innovations and practical solutions with tangible economic and societal impact.
    She noted that the Cultural Mission’s efforts extend beyond academic supervision to identifying national talent, showcasing their accomplishments, and fostering connections with academic and research institutions, as well as other relevant sectors. This opens broader horizons for developing their innovations and translating them into practical applications that serve the nation.
    She stressed that the true value of the scholarship program is not measured solely by the number of graduates, but by the knowledge they produce, the innovations they introduce, and the impact they leave on the nation’s development journey. She pointed out that these exemplary individuals reflect the promising potential of Saudi scholarship students and their role in strengthening the Kingdom’s global presence in science and research.
    In her concluding remarks, she affirmed that the Cultural Mission will continue its efforts to support both male and female scholarship students, highlight their scientific and innovative achievements, and maximize opportunities to leverage their work for knowledge transfer, technology localization, and the advancement of the Kingdom’s development priorities—all in line with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030.
    -- SPA
